observation_summary: The compiler fails to remove unused classes when they are used with goog.addSingletonGetter, because the inlining process incorrectly modifies the code structure in a way that prevents subsequent dead-code elimination.
hypothesis: The InlineVariables pass is too aggressive in inlining singleton getter calls, which obscures the class structure and prevents the NameAnalyzer from identifying the class as unused. Adding a guard to prevent inlining when a singleton getter is detected will preserve the necessary structure for dead-code removal.
prediction: Adding a check in InlineVariables to detect if a call is a singleton getter and returning false (preventing inlining) will allow the compiler to correctly identify and remove the unused class.
experiment_rationale: The fix diff explicitly adds a conditional check (`if (convention.getSingletonGetterClassName(callNode) != null)`) to prevent inlining, which directly addresses the root cause identified in the bug report comments.
reasoning_summary: The bug is caused by an overly aggressive inlining strategy that breaks the assumptions of the dead-code elimination pass. The fix is to add a guard (a check) to prevent this specific inlining behavior, which fits the definition of a 'Checking' defect (missing validation/guard).

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the inlining logic is part of an algorithm, the specific fix is the addition of a guard condition to prevent the algorithm from executing in an invalid state, which is the hallmark of a Checking defect.
